newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends weak as U.S. gasoline slides.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends weak as U.S. gasoline slides.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed weaker and near session lows posted late on Wednesday after a day dominated by evidence of slack U.S. gasoline demand which sent New York markets tumbling, brokers said.

NYMEX May unleaded gasoline shed two cents a gallon at one stage after the American Petroleum Institute (API) predicted supply would be more than adequate to meet peak summer demand, even if the most bullish growth forecasts were fulfilled.
May Brent closed 33 cents weaker at $17.81 a barrel, following gasoline's lead but also taking a beating from reports of a big build in U.S. crude inventories last week.

API and U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) data showed U.S. crude stocks rose for a sixth consecutive week, climbing by between 2.5 and three million barrels. In the key U.S. Gulf refining region, crude stocks are now 11.3 million barrels above year-ago levels.
"It's been mostly about the stocks today but we also broke through some technical support," said a broker.
Dealers said the failure of support to hold on June Brent at $17.91 and on May WTI crude at $19.45 gave added impetus to the afternoon's slide.
The June Brent-WTI spread lost 15 cents to end at $1.37.
Earlier, IPE gas oil futures closed weaker, also taking their lead from the U.S. inventory data, brokers said.
May gas oil closed $2.75 a tonne lower at $162.50, off a session high of $163.75.

DOE and API data showed middle distillate stocks rose by between 1.6 million and 2.5 million barrels last week, defying some traders expectations of a fall due to unseasonably cold weather in the U.S. Northeast.
Nevertheless, some brokers drew encouragement from the May contract's close above support at $162.25 and $162 a tonne.
